content:
{'translation': "Apple's highly anticipated AI smart glasses, expected to launch late next year, finally have a projected unveiling date.", 'index': 0}

{'translation': 'WWDC27 亮相', 'index': 1}

{'translation': 'Earlier this year there were reports suggesting Apple\'s AI smart glasses should be available for consumers to purchase by the end of 2027. According to a report today from Bloomberg journalist Mark Gurman, that still appears to be the case. However, we now know that Apple is "currently targeting" unveiling the new glasses to the public at next year\'s Worldwide Developers Conference.', 'index': 2}

{'translation': "The timing of this unveiling may hint at the future direction of Apple's AI glasses. Apple seems unlikely to introduce a new device at WWDC without offering developers any way to build software for it. As such, the glasses may be able to draw in third-party app data and actions, much like the new Siri AI, rather than being limited to Apple's own features.", 'index': 3}

{'translation': 'If true, the whole process would be very similar to the 2023 unveiling of the Apple Vision Pro: hardware and software previewed months ahead, giving developers time to build apps for the platform, with the hardware itself going on sale later.', 'index': 4}

{'translation': '私隱爭議', 'index': 5}

{'translation': "One of the reasons Apple's glasses have been pushed back repeatedly from their originally expected late-2026 launch is the company's ongoing efforts to address privacy concerns. Existing products from the likes of Meta have drawn criticism, opposition, and even outright bans over concerns about the privacy implications of glasses fitted with cameras. According to Gurman's report, Apple is exploring several approaches. As well as testing devices with no cameras at all, Apple is also weighing up software solutions:", 'index': 6}

{'translation': 'Beyond that, Apple is also reportedly "developing a number of new privacy features, both hardware- and software-related, that are not present on any current products."', 'index': 7}

{'translation': '總結', 'index': 8}

{'translation': "Apple's AI glasses will not feature any display, but are expected to be capable of taking photos, playing music, conversing with Siri, taking calls, and much more. The product is also said to sport a distinctive, stylish design to set it apart from competitors. Does this product pique your interest? Let us know in the comments!", 'index': 9}
